mission_06: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) is a quasi-experimental method that compares the change in outcomes over time between a treatment group and a control group. The key identifying assumption is parallel trends: in the absence of treatment, the average outcomes for treated and control groups would have followed parallel paths. The classic 2x2 DiD estimator computes the difference in before-after changes between groups. The two-way fixed effects (TWFE) regression extends this to panel data with multiple periods: Y_it = α + β(Treat_i × Post_t) + γ_i + δ_t + ε_it, where γ_i and δ_t are unit and time fixed effects. You will also implement parallel trends tests using pre-treatment periods and event study specifications that estimate dynamic treatment effects over time, revealing how effects evolve after treatment.
